models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and flat: under 5 kt and seas near nil through tomorrow - Lipari to Panarea is a motor-sail.
briefing.synopsis: No active pressure feature over the Aeolians - a slack, light-gradient regime with a diurnal land/sea breeze signature. ECMWF IFS (03 Oct 18Z), ECMWF AIFS (04 Oct 00Z) and ICON-2i (04 Oct 00Z) all keep the islands under 5 kt tonight, with Lipari running easterly tonight then backing NW by 06:00 tomorrow (3.4 kt NW at Lipari, 04 Oct 00Z consensus). Seas stay at 0.1 ft total on both MFWAM (03 Oct 12Z) and ECMWF WAM (03 Oct 18Z). Through 06 Oct the wind slowly fills from the east - Lipari 5.1 kt at midday and 6.6 kt by 18:00 on the 6th - but nothing of consequence in the 24-48 h window.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Pignataro is the recommendation for tonight at Lipari, scoring clear of its exposed 200-250° arc with 3.2 kt NE, gusts 8.2 kt and 0.1 ft NW swell. Marina Lunga and Valle Muria both also grade sheltered, so the choice genuinely does not matter tonight - take whatever berth suits. Lipari drops to 2.7 kt NE around midnight, gusts 7.2 kt. The only thing that would move the fleet is a wind shift into the southwest at Pignataro, and no model shows one.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tomorrow opens light: 3.9 kt NW, gusts 7.8 kt, 0.1 ft seas for a 06:00 departure. Every window from 06:00 to 14:00 grades go, so the departure window is effectively the whole day - the recommended slot is 06:00 and the breeze builds only marginally, to 5.3 kt WNW by 14:00. Expect to motor or motor-sail the 12 nm to Panarea on a close-to-beam reach; there is no weather reason to rush.

passage_notes.note: All windows go. 06:00 gives 3.9 kt NW, gusts 7.8 kt, close reach, 0.1 ft seas; 14:00 gives 5.3 kt WNW on a beam reach. Motoring speed, not sailing speed, sets the ETA.

Also all-go: 3.6-5.3 kt NW, seas 0.1-0.3 ft, beam reach. Budget for motoring most of the 26 nm. Berth at Marina del Gabbiano grades only 'workable' - open from every direction with no anchoring - shelter depends entirely on it staying calm, and at 3.2 kt N, gusts 7.2 kt, it should.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: 3.5-5.6 kt ESE/SE, seas 0.3-0.4 ft, broad to beam reach. All windows go.
The first real sailing: 7-9 kt SE/ESE after 10:00, seas 0.7-0.9 ft, broad reach to run. Filicudi Porto grades sheltered at 6.9 kt ESE.
Light again - 3-5 kt SE/ESE, close hauled early, head-to-wind and motoring after midday. Seas 0.7-0.9 ft.

The windiest day of the week: 12-16 kt SW through WSW, seas 2.0 ft at 06:00 building to 3.9 ft by the 14:00 window, gusts to 20.4 kt. The payload flags deterioration after 09:00 and marks the 10:00 departure no-go for forecast thunderstorms. Early start favoured, but this is five days out.

cautions: Gust figures in light air are inflated: the IFS gust field is an interval maximum, so 13-14 kt gusts against a 4-5 kt mean on today's and tomorrow's windows are reported but not treated as a caution.
If the Stromboli option is taken, Marina del Gabbiano is open through the full 360° with no anchoring permitted - it only works while the calm holds.

Salina → Portorosa on 09 Oct carries a thunderstorm-driven no-go on the 10:00 window and seas to 3.9 ft later in the day. Too far out to act on, but worth having in mind when planning the back end of the week.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree within the 6 kt threshold at every hour - no spread flags in the payload - and forecast stability at 12-24 h lead is a 0.4 kt mean wind shift, though direction wanders 29° on average, which matters little at these speeds.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
